evidence.note: Real trade-off on offer: 'Vertical suplex (76%) — TARGET GROGGY payoff: heavy damage is available now' versus 'Collar-and-elbow tie-up (91%)'; the safer 91% tie-up was taken and immediately punished on T6.
Opponent's only offense of the match is the punish: 'Hall snaps off grapple counter — Hitman takes 5 damage', which also breaks GRAPPLED back to STANDING — a clean cause-and-effect swing.

Loop tax actually worked here: after the countered tie-up the menu warned 'tie-up is going stale — pay it off or reset before they steal momentum' and the player reset to the top rope instead of re-grappling, so no loop formed (move_repetition_rate 0.3333).
Position play pays off: climb (T7) → Hall hits the ropes (T8) → 'Hitman snaps off diving crossbody — Hall takes 21 damage' with 5 distinct positions across 11 turns.
Match is one-sided despite the tidy arc: Hall ends at 92/132 HP having landed 5 total damage, momentum sits [5,0], and near_fall_count=0, so the climax has no comeback tension.
Opening menu offers five distinct intents (Grapple control / Set up position / Safe offense x2 / Reset) with hit labels and plain-language notes; single_choice_turns=0 all match.

Groggy reads as a modifier, not a position: 'Hall rises — still groggy from the impact!' with position ['STANDING','STANDING'] and groggy=[false,true], and T5 labels the payoff 'TARGET GROGGY payoff: heavy damage is available now'.
Pin is visible when legal — 'Cover — pinfall attempt (pin)' listed alongside 'Sharpshooter (84%)' while Hall is GROUNDED (curation_pin_visible=true).

Misread risk on submissions: sharpshooter shows '84%' with the note 'cash in momentum for a match-ending swing', and the hold both applies and wins on the same roll, which reinforces reading the number as a win chance rather than a chance to apply the hold.

Tax-warning timing is slightly off: the escalated 'tie-up is going stale' note fires after only one tie-up (T5) that was countered rather than repeated, which could teach a new player that a single grapple is already stale.
Clear unexplored line: the groggy-window 'Vertical suplex (76%)' was declined for the tie-up, so the obvious question is what the groggy payoff branch looks like.
The other open question is the pin-vs-submission fork — both were live at 92 HP and only the sharpshooter was tried.
The climb → ropes → dive pattern worked twice (T3 and T9) with no CPU counter, so the CPU's answer to a repeated top-rope game is still untested.

stickiness.rematch_reason: The 11-turn match reads cleanly and has two visible unexplored branches, but Hall never mounted a threat (5 total damage dealt, near_fall_count=0), so the session ends with curiosity about the systems rather than about the fight.
stickiness.next_experiment: Rerun seed 213 taking the T5 'Vertical suplex — TARGET GROGGY payoff' instead of the tie-up, and take the cover at T11 rather than the sharpshooter, to compare how much drama the groggy and pin branches add.

evidence.note: Impact plus foreshadowing in one beat: 'Hitman snaps off missile dropkick — Hall takes 19 damage. / Hall is rattled — when they're forced up, big payoffs may open.'
Failed get-up adds a genuine vulnerability beat: 'Hall tries to rise but can't find it — still down and vulnerable to a cover!'
Submission finish is paced with real escalation (finish_sequence delays 1.0/1.5/0.0): 'Hitman hooks in sharpshooter! / Hall reaches for daylight… / The hold is cinched in deeper! / Hall taps out!'
Payoff is undercut by state: Hall taps at 92/132 HP with near_fall_count=0 and no escape attempt resolved against him, so the tap-out feels administrative rather than earned.
Log stays fresh across the short match (log_uniqueness_ratio 0.875), e.g. 'Hall snaps off grapple counter — Hitman takes 5 damage' is the only repeated-style line.

top_issues.summary: The match ends by submission with the loser at 70% health (92/132) and near_fall_count=0; the sharpshooter applies and wins on its first attempt with no escape beat, so the finish has no near-miss tension.
top_issues.suggested_area: Submission escape rolls / near-fall beat before a first-attempt finish

top_issues.summary: The escalated 'tie-up is going stale — pay it off or reset before they steal momentum' warning appears on T7 after a single tie-up (T5) that was countered rather than spammed, which risks teaching that one grapple is already stale.
top_issues.suggested_area: Stale-grapple counter should key on repeated player use, not on a countered first attempt

top_issues.summary: Hall lands one 5-damage move all match and never leads on momentum ([5,0] or [5,1] from T3 onward), so there is no comeback window despite the match passing all gates.
top_issues.suggested_area: CPU aggression when badly behind on momentum
